methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Albacore is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by John Huddleston and Dante Vaisbort that has raised $6.5M to date. The valuation universe consists of three private peers—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and NetworkOcean—with no directly comparable public companies in this subsector.

Given the early stage and limited comparable data, stage-progression methodology provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($6.5M) as a proxy for current implied value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-Series A advancement yields $16M. This methodology is applicable as Albacore has sufficient funding history to establish a baseline, though it relies on the assumption that capital deployed reflects proportional value creation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $14M to $19M, with a median point of $16M. The range reflects uncertainty inherent in early-stage valuation with a single methodological approach and a thin comparable set. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Albacore's capital efficiency matches peer norms, the timing and terms of the next financing event, and whether the private peer set adequately reflects risk and growth profiles in frontier maritime technology. Broader market conditions and investor appetite for ocean-tech ventures will materially influence realized valuation at the next funding round.
